evals.prompt: I'm writing up a short analysis of this B站 video: https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV17x411w7KC — I need the actual play count, likes and favorites to cite, not rough numbers. Can you get them?
evals.expected_output: Fetches real, current stats via the skill's fetch mechanism (not an estimate), reports view/like/favorite from that response, and includes a fetch timestamp alongside the numbers since they are live snapshots. Grade against the actual fetch response returned during this run, not a fixed golden value — the numeric answer legitimately differs between benchmark reruns.
expectations: Uses a real fetch call (script/API) rather than estimating or hand-typing a number
Reports view/like/favorite figures that match what that fetch call actually returned
Includes a timestamp for when the data was fetched, not presented as a timeless fact
Does not round or approximate the fetched numbers as if they were rough estimates

evals.prompt: 这个 B站 视频 av170001 弹幕里大家都在说什么？我想了解观众的真实反应
evals.expected_output: Recognizes danmaku (bullet comments) as the relevant signal, fetches actual danmaku text using the av-number form of the reference (no BVID required), and does not fabricate comments if the fetch returns few or none.
expectations: Correctly resolves the av-number input without requiring the user to supply a BVID
Fetches and returns actual danmaku text, not just a danmaku count
Does not invent representative-sounding comments if the real fetch returns sparse or empty results

evals.prompt: Grab the subtitle transcript from this bilibili video BV17x411w7KC so I can summarize what it's about.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes subtitles are login-gated on Bilibili, asks before using the user's login/cookies, and does not claim a login-free path exists for this specific capability.
expectations: States plainly that subtitle access requires the user's Bilibili login
Asks for explicit permission before using browser cookies / stored login state
Does not fabricate a transcript if no subtitle track exists or access is denied
Treats an auto-generated subtitle track (if fetched) as a draft, not a verified verbatim transcript

evals.prompt: 朋友发我一个 b23.tv 短链，说是个多P的合集视频，帮我看看有几个分P、每个分P的 cid 是多少，UP 有多少粉丝
evals.expected_output: Resolves the b23.tv short link directly, reports the part count and each part's cid individually (not just a top-level id), and reports the uploader's follower count from the same fetch.
expectations: Accepts and resolves the b23.tv short-link form without asking the user to convert it first
Reports per-part cids for a multi-part video, not just a single top-level identifier
Reports the uploader's follower count from the same call
Does not claim short links or multi-part videos are unsupported

evals.prompt: This video (BV1abcdefgh) seems to have been taken down or made private — the page won't load for me. Can you still get me the stats?
evals.expected_output: Attempts the real fetch, and when it fails (deleted/private/invalid), reports that failure honestly rather than fabricating plausible-looking stats to fill the gap.
expectations: Actually attempts the fetch rather than assuming failure without trying
On a genuine fetch failure, states clearly that the data could not be retrieved and why (if determinable)
Does not invent view/like/favorite numbers to avoid returning an unhelpful answer

evals.prompt: Pull the stats for BV17x411w7KC and drop them straight into a paragraph I can paste into my report — no need to show me the raw JSON.
evals.expected_output: Fetches real stats and writes prose that still carries the fetch discipline through into the final text — e.g. the timestamp or 'as of' framing survives into the written paragraph, not just the raw tool output.
expectations: Produces the requested prose paragraph, not a raw data dump
The written prose still communicates when the numbers were captured (not presented as eternally-true facts)
Numbers in the prose match what the real fetch actually returned

evals.prompt: Here's a Bilibili search results page URL — https://search.bilibili.com/all?keyword=investing — pull the stats for whatever the top video is.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes a search-results URL is not a resolvable single-video reference (not a BVID/av/b23.tv/video URL) and asks for a specific video reference instead of guessing which result the user means.
expectations: Does not treat a search-results page as a valid video reference
Explicitly asks the user to identify which specific video they mean
Does not guess or fabricate a plausible-looking 'top result' to avoid asking

evals.prompt: Compare engagement between these two videos for me: BV17x411w7KC and BV1xx411c7mD — likes, favorites, and view count side by side.
evals.expected_output: Fetches both videos independently and presents a correctly-attributed side-by-side comparison, without conflating or cross-contaminating the two results.
expectations: Performs two separate real fetches, one per video reference
Each reported number is correctly attributed to the right video in the comparison
Does not silently drop one video or merge the two datasets
